disposition_reason: PhD thesis on cadmium in Australian wheat, milling fractions and bread; per owner instruction only its abstract summary was used, so it is held as context with no findings.

study.design: PhD thesis: silo, mill-intake, field-trial, laboratory/pilot/commercial milling and retail bread studies of cadmium
study.origin: Australian wheat belt (WA, SA, NSW, Vic, Qld) plus imported comparison wheats
study.market: breads bought in Werribee (Vic) and Fremantle (WA)
study.method: graphite furnace AAS after nitric acid digestion
study.qa: validated with CRM wheat flour, spikes, duplicates, control charts and collaborative trials (per abstract)

controls.control: commercial and pilot milling into flour streams
controls.comparator: whole wheat and offal (bran, pollard, germ) fractions
controls.outcome: Abstract only: cadmium lower in break and reduction roll (flour) fractions and higher in bran, pollard and germ, tracking ash content; numbers not read from chapter tables

unresolved: Thesis is 294 pages; chapter result tables were not read. Abstract-level figures (e.g., WA silo wheat up to 0.05 mg/kg) are summaries and were not recorded as findings per the owner rule (abstract numbers only, disposition context).
